title: Act Before Certainty
goal: Commit the public-response thresholds before the next orbit update exists, then be held to them.
world: a response board with blank threshold rows
the current impact probability and its date of issue
lead times for each staged action, posted next to it
no preview of the incoming updates
actions: write a threshold, an owner and an action for each response stage
set the lead time each stage needs to be possible at all
release the board and receive the scripted probability updates
execute the stage the player's own rule fires, or override and account for it

conditions.label: Public advisory
conditions.action: Publish the corridor and the uncertainty

conditions.label: Stage regional resources
conditions.action: Move shelter and transport capacity into the corridor

stream.update: probability 1 in 310 after radar; nominal miss moves away
probability 1 in 40; corridor narrows to two provinces
probability 1 in 9000 after the fourth tracking pass

success: Every stage the player's own thresholds fired was executed at a moment when its lead time still made it possible, and the day-15 fall does not retroactively make the day-9 action wrong.

failures.action: Thresholds written after seeing the day-4 update
failures.consequence: The board is timestamped; the rule that fires is the one written first
failures.line: You wrote that after the number moved. That is not a threshold, that is a reaction.

failures.action: Evacuation threshold set below the 336-hour lead time
failures.consequence: The rule fires on day 9 and the action is already impossible
failures.line: The rule is correct. We needed it fourteen days ago.

failures.action: Overriding a fired threshold because the probability feels low
failures.consequence: Later dialogue records the override and the loss of the board's authority
failures.line: Then nobody has to believe the next one either.

followup.prompt: Why did the day-15 drop to 1 in 9000 not make the day-9 decision a mistake?
followup.answer: The decision was correct on the information available and on a rule written before it; a later narrowing of the uncertainty changes what to do next, not whether the earlier action was justified.

assumes: a probability is a statement about knowledge, not about the asteroid
staged responses have lead times that are not compressible

title: Buy the Failure You Actually Remove
goal: Spend the one major yard slot on the refit that removes a causal path this boat has actually walked down.
world: the patrol casualty log, event by event
the measured one-scrubber atmosphere margin at twenty hours
the next patrol's mission profile
four refit proposals with specifications, no ranking
actions: tag each logged event by recurrence, consequence and capability affected
open each proposal and mark which causal path it removes and which metric it merely improves
apply the next-patrol profile to weight the exposures
commit the slot and defend it from the log

data.decision: which failure the next patrol will not repeat

options.label: Independent navigation reference on a separate physical chain
Redundant navigation sensor on the existing inertial feed

success: The player selects the refit that changes a stated next-patrol decision and cites the log, rather than the proposal with the largest specification number.

failures.action: Choosing the larger drain pump
failures.consequence: The log shows every flooding event was bounded by source isolation, not by pump capacity
failures.line: Show me the entry where a bigger pump would have changed the outcome.

failures.action: Choosing atmosphere capacity
failures.consequence: The measured twenty-hour margin is compared against a four-hour quiet window
failures.line: I have twenty hours. I needed four.

failures.action: Choosing the redundant sensor on the same feed
failures.consequence: The dependency view shows the new sensor inheriting the failed source
failures.line: Independent of what?

followup.prompt: What made the best refit mission-specific rather than universally best?
followup.answer: Its value depended on which failure had recurred, what consequence it caused, what the next patrol would expose the boat to, and whether the proposal removed that causal path rather than improving a number beside it.

assumes: a specification improvement is not the same as a removed failure mode

title: Fit the Entry Cloud Inside the Corridor
goal: Judge entry readiness from the distribution of possible trajectories rather than from one nominal angle.
world: the 5.3 to 7.7 degree corridor drawn on the entry display
a cloud of entry-angle samples generated from the current state uncertainty
separate toggles for atmospheric density and centre-of-mass assumptions
the cost in hours of each available action
actions: read how many samples currently fall outside the corridor
move the nominal target angle and watch the cloud move with it
add a tracking observation and watch the cloud narrow
toggle the survivability assumptions and see the boundary move independently of navigation
choose between another correction and another observation

actions.label: Retarget the nominal to corridor centre

success: The player distinguishes moving the nominal from reducing the uncertainty, and recognises the shallow side as the tighter margin in the current solution.

failures.action: Retargeting to corridor centre and calling it ready
failures.consequence: The same fraction of trajectories sits outside the corridor, now split across both edges
failures.line: You moved the dot. The cloud came with it.

failures.action: Reading only the nominal angle
failures.consequence: The nominal sits comfortably inside while the shallow tail does not
failures.line: That angle is the one place we are least likely to actually be.

followup.prompt: What did the new tracking pass buy that recentring the nominal did not?
followup.answer: It narrowed the range of plausible actual trajectories, so fewer of them lie outside the corridor; recentring only relabelled which trajectory is called nominal.

assumes: a state estimate is a distribution, not a point
corridor limits come from survivability physics, not from navigation

title: Build the River Sampling Plan
goal: Spend twenty laboratory slots on the plan that can answer the question the city is actually asking.
world: a physical crate holding exactly twenty slots
the river map with intake, upstream and downstream marked
the partition model's prediction posted on the wall beside it
no recommended plan anywhere
actions: allocate slots among water, suspended solids, sediment cores, repeats and times
read the panel showing which questions the current plan can and cannot answer
commit the crate

answers.question: Is the intake water above the release criterion today?
Is the river carrying it dissolved or on particles?
Is there a reservoir that will keep releasing it after the plume passes?
Is the concentration rising or falling?

success: The plan is feasible, keeps its protected slots, and the player can say which of the four questions it answers and which it does not.

failures.action: A water-only plan
failures.consequence: Results come back reassuring; a later scripted check opens an unsampled sediment core
failures.line: Which phase did you actually sample?

failures.action: Spending every slot on coverage
failures.consequence: No blanks or replicates, so no result can be defended
failures.line: Twenty numbers and nothing that says any of them is real.

followup.prompt: Your plan cannot answer one of the four questions. Which, and what would you give up to buy it?
followup.answer: Naming the unanswered question and the specific trade is the answer; sampling design is experimental design under a budget, and every plan forgoes something.

assumes: a contaminant partitions between water, particles and sediment
a measurement without a blank cannot be defended

title: Close the 62-Hour Power Ledger
goal: Build a duty-cycle schedule that fits the remaining amp-hour allocation and still has reserve at entry.
world: the remaining allocation in amp-hours, on the bus panel
each load shown as current draw against a timeline, not as a switch
the required communication and guidance windows, marked on the timeline
local battery temperature, and its effect on usable capacity
actions: schedule each load into the hours it is actually needed
choose low-rate communications between the required windows
set a minimum thermal-control duty cycle and watch capacity respond
hold back a protected reserve for entry

answers.question: Does the schedule fit the allocation across all 62 hours?
Is there reserve left for one missed assumption?

success: Integrated amp-hours stay under the allocation, protected loads are satisfied in their windows, and reserve survives to entry.

failures.action: Switching off the single biggest load and declaring it solved
failures.consequence: The instantaneous draw looks good; the integral crosses the allocation at hour 51
failures.line: You saved watts. I asked you to save watt-hours.

failures.action: Securing thermal control to buy margin
failures.consequence: Local battery temperature falls and usable capacity drops, costing more than the load saved
failures.line: The battery is colder than the cabin. It always was.

followup.prompt: Why is turn off the biggest load not a complete power strategy?
followup.answer: Mission functions are needed at different times, so the governing quantity is integrated energy across the whole horizon, plus the consequence each switch-off starts somewhere else.

assumes: energy is power integrated over time
battery capability depends on the battery's own temperature

title: The Wrong Zero
goal: Find the mislabelled denominator and correct exactly the conclusions that used it.
world: five days of paired recordings from the old vault and the temporary rock station
the spectral band the Flats ratio was computed in
the published Flats-over-vault ratio near 3
a dependency graph, initially collapsed
actions: overlay the paired recordings and compare amplitudes in the working band
measure the vault-over-rock factor
recompute the Flats-over-rock ratio
open the dependency graph and mark every conclusion that used the vault as reference

resources.label: Old vault treated as competent-rock reference

success: The affected site-response ratios are corrected to about 4.8 while the direct observations and independent instruments keep their evidential value.

failures.action: Multiplying every earthquake quantity by 1.6
failures.consequence: The dependency graph rejects the magnitude and the direct building measurements
failures.line: The numerator was measured correctly. The label on the denominator was wrong.

failures.action: Discarding the whole fortnight of Flats data
failures.consequence: Correctly measured amplitudes are thrown away with the bad reference
failures.line: You just deleted the only record of what the fill did.

followup.prompt: Why is tracing dependencies better than declaring the fortnight wrong?
followup.answer: The reference error biases only the conclusions that used it as a denominator; unrelated observations and independent instruments are untouched and still carry evidence.

assumes: a site-response ratio is a comparison, so it inherits the reference's error
independent means a different physical measurement chain, not a different display

title: A Signature Is Not the Check
goal: Close the rig-for-dive checklist with present evidence behind every critical claim.
world: the checklist, already signed
hull valves, bilges, escape routes and pump test stations, physically walkable
the maintenance log and the switchboard, which disagree on one item
the watch bill showing who was aboard, and when
actions: walk to a claimed item and perform or inspect the evidence for it
compare the switchboard indication, the log entry and the direct circuit condition
flag a signature that could not have been made
assign discrepant items for re-verification, then close the boat

claims.label: Breaker 2B isolated
claims.evidence_kind: log says isolated, circuit reads energized

claims.label: Drain pump tested
claims.evidence_kind: impossible — ashore on the signed date

success: Signature-as-proof is rejected, the three discrepant critical items are re-verified, and each closed claim is linked to evidence taken now.

failures.action: Accepting the signatures and closing the boat
failures.consequence: The blocked route and the live circuit persist into the simulated dive
failures.line: The list records who is responsible. It does not record what is true.

failures.action: Believing the log over the measured circuit
failures.consequence: The discrepancy stays open and closeout is refused
failures.line: One of these was written. The other was measured.

failures.action: Re-checking every item on the list
failures.consequence: The clock runs out before the critical three are reached
failures.line: You have time to verify what matters or time to verify everything. Not both.

followup.prompt: What is the difference between a checklist signature and the evidence the checklist is supposed to preserve?
followup.answer: The signature records responsibility; the evidence demonstrates that the physical condition was actually verified, by someone who was there, at a time that still applies.

assumes: an indication reports a commanded state, not a measured condition

title: Make the Noise Follow One Machine
goal: Establish which machine is producing the new tone, and prove it by reversal.
world: a broadband rise on all bearings
a new machinery-order tone with a readable frequency
the plant event log for the hour the noise appeared
four candidate machines, none marked
actions: ask sonar for the tone frequency and how it tracks machinery rate
change one candidate machine state while holding the other three fixed
have sonar report amplitude and frequency after each change
restore the suspect machine and confirm the feature returns
success: One reproducible machine-to-tone relationship is isolated and confirmed by restoring the machine and hearing the line come back.

failures.action: Securing several machines at once
failures.consequence: The display goes quiet and no causal relationship has been established
failures.line: Quieter. Not answered.

failures.action: Naming the machine that was started most recently, without reversal
failures.consequence: The coincidence stands unchallenged and returns in a later mission
failures.line: That is when it started. That is not why.

failures.action: Reading the small frequency offset as target Doppler
failures.consequence: The source is on the same hull as the hydrophones, so there is no relative motion to Doppler-shift
failures.line: Doppler between what and what?

followup.prompt: Why did restoring the suspect machine and hearing the line return matter?
followup.answer: The reversal made the relationship reproducible in both directions, which separates a causal machine state from a change that merely coincided with it.

assumes: a controlled test changes one variable and holds the rest
a machinery-order tone scales with the machine's rate

title: Draw the Source
goal: Locate the source from three stations, and see what a clock error does to the geometry.
world: three station traces with pickable P and S arrivals
the crustal rule of thumb posted at the workstation
the regional map, with the stations on it
a clock-drift correction for one station, switchable
actions: pick the P and S arrivals on each trace
convert each S-minus-P interval to a distance
draw the radius around each station
toggle the clock-drift correction and watch one circle move
success: The source is located from the intersection of three constraints, and the player can say that one station gives a distance, three give a region, and a timing error moves the geometry without changing any waveform.

failures.action: Using one station
failures.consequence: An entire ring of possible sources remains
failures.line: That is how far. I asked where.

failures.action: Using magnitude as the radius
failures.consequence: The circles do not intersect anywhere plausible
failures.line: That number says how big.

failures.action: Reporting the overlap as a point
failures.consequence: The region has area and the report claims precision it does not have
failures.line: Give me the region. I will decide what to do with its edges.

followup.prompt: Why does correcting a station clock move the epicentre when the waveform shape is unchanged?
followup.answer: The location is computed from arrival times; a clock bias changes the inferred travel-time difference and therefore that station's distance, which translates the intersection.

assumes: S and P waves travel at different speeds, so their separation grows with distance

title: Break the Brightness Degeneracy
goal: Discover that reflected brightness fixes a family of diameter-albedo pairs, and watch different physics collapse it.
world: the measured visual brightness at the observed distance
a diameter control and an albedo control
a live plot of which combinations reproduce the brightness
a thermal-infrared observation, available but not yet applied
actions: move diameter and albedo and watch the brightness stay matched along a locus
note that the locus spans a factor of several in diameter
apply the thermal data and watch the family collapse
read the surviving diameter and state what is now measured and what is still inferred

observable.label: Absolute visual magnitude
observable.locus: diameter proportional to albedo^-0.5 at fixed brightness

second.label: Thermal infrared flux
second.physics: re-emitted absorbed sunlight, so it scales with area and with 1 minus albedo

success: The player sees a two-dimensional family reduce to a point when a measurement based on different physics arrives, and keeps diameter as measured while density and strength stay inferred.

failures.action: Picking a diameter from brightness alone
failures.consequence: Any diameter on the locus fits, and the choice is unjustified
failures.line: Give me the albedo you assumed and I will give you any size you like.

failures.action: Treating the spectral class as a density
failures.consequence: Adebayo blocks the silent conversion from taxonomy to bulk property
failures.line: That is a surface. You are about to use it as an interior.

followup.prompt: Why did thermal infrared break the tie when another optical image would not have?
followup.answer: Thermal flux depends on absorbed sunlight, so it responds to albedo in the opposite sense to reflected light; a second measurement with the same dependence would slide along the same locus.

assumes: reflected brightness depends on the product of area and albedo
absorbed and reflected fractions sum to one

title: Trace the Gym's Force
goal: Follow lateral force from the roof to the ground and name the transfer that governs.
world: the gym, walkable from roof diaphragm to foundation
a load-path tracer that highlights only what the player has already identified
the classroom block next door, with shorter redundant wall paths
the roof-to-panel anchors, small and unremarkable
actions: stand at each interface and name what physically transfers lateral force
follow the path without skipping an interface
compare with the classroom block's redundant paths
flag the transfer whose failure leaves a heavy panel unsupported out of plane

links.label: Roof deck acting as diaphragm
links.transfers: roof inertia into the plane of the roof

links.label: Collector member
links.transfers: diaphragm shear to the resisting line

links.label: Roof-to-panel anchor
links.transfers: panel and roof inertia across the joint

success: A continuous path is completed with no interface skipped, and the anchor is named as the governing transfer with its capacity flagged as untested.

failures.action: Jumping from roof to ground
failures.consequence: The tracer leaves a gap and refuses to close the path
failures.line: Point at the thing that carries it across.

failures.action: Naming the panel because it is the largest element
failures.consequence: No capacity measurement exists for the transfer that would actually fail
failures.line: The panel is not the question. What load can I put on the tie?

followup.prompt: Why can a small anchor control the safety of a very large wall panel?
followup.answer: A load path is limited by its weakest required transfer; if the connection cannot pass the inertia into the resisting system, the panel's own material strength cannot rescue a broken path.

assumes: lateral force must reach the ground through a continuous set of physical connections

title: Find the Hole Before the Pump Loses
goal: Identify the source and account for the whole inflow, including what the running pump has already removed.
world: bilge level markings, readable to the centimetre
the flooded deck area posted on the compartment plan
the drain pump running, with its discharge rate on the gauge
conductivity references for outside seawater and for fresh water
fresh-water tank level and sonar-cooling return pressure
actions: sample the bilge and compare conductivity with both references
check the neighbouring system indications
mark the level, wait one minute, read it again
combine the rise, the area and the pump discharge
isolate at the boundary and watch the trend reverse

streams.label: Accumulation in the bilge
streams.measured: 8 cm rise over 4.0 m2 in one minute = 320 L/min

hidden.label: The pump has been running the whole time

success: The sea-connected source is identified from conductivity, the inflow is estimated near 410 L/min, and the pressure source is isolated rather than answered with more pumps.

failures.action: Reporting 320 L/min as the leak rate
failures.consequence: The estimate ignores everything the pump removed during the measurement
failures.line: That is what got past the pump.

failures.action: Starting another pump
failures.consequence: The rise slows and the source stays open
failures.line: Where is the pressure coming from?

failures.action: Closing an unrelated fresh-water line
failures.consequence: A service is lost and the bilge keeps rising
failures.line: Check what you just isolated against what you measured.

followup.prompt: Why was the leak rate larger than the rate at which the bilge level rose?
followup.answer: The observed rise was what remained after the pump removed 90 litres a minute; the actual inflow is accumulation plus everything already discharged.

assumes: a volume rate is a level rate times a plan area
conductivity distinguishes seawater from a fresh-water system

title: Measure the Nudge
goal: Predict the momentum transfer, deliver it, and then measure whether the orbit actually changed by that much.
world: the spacecraft mass and closing speed on the mission board
the target's measured diameter and its inferred density, labelled differently
an ejecta-enhancement factor with a stated range, not a value
the pre-impact orbit solution, with its uncertainty
tracking time available after impact, in a finite budget
actions: predict the direct momentum transfer
state the enhancement range and the resulting delta-v range
establish the pre-impact orbit to a stated precision
commit the impact
choose whether to spend the post-impact tracking, then refit the orbit
compare the measured change with the prediction
success: A delta-v range is predicted with the enhancement uncertainty carried, the impact is delivered, and the post-impact orbit is measured so that prediction and outcome can be compared.

failures.action: Declaring success on confirmed impact
failures.consequence: The campaign ends with no measured deflection and no way to know whether it worked
failures.line: We hit it. Nobody has told me what moved.

failures.action: Predicting a single delta-v with no enhancement range
failures.consequence: The measured value lands outside the stated prediction and there is no honest way to report it
failures.line: Which of your assumptions carried that number?

failures.action: Spending the tracking budget before impact
failures.consequence: The pre-impact orbit is beautiful and there is nothing left to measure the change with
failures.line: Both orbits, or neither.

followup.prompt: Why is a confirmed impact not a confirmed deflection?
followup.answer: Momentum transfer depends on ejecta as well as the spacecraft, and that enhancement is uncertain by a large factor; only measuring the post-impact orbit tests whether the transfer was what the model predicted.

assumes: momentum is conserved, and ejecta leaving the surface carries some of it
an orbital period change is measurable by tracking

title: Which Number Is Carrying the Error
goal: Propagate the input uncertainties into impact energy and decide which measurement is worth buying.
world: measured diameter with its stated uncertainty
inferred density with a much wider range, labelled inferred
approach speed, and the entry speed derived from it
a live contribution bar for each input's share of the output uncertainty
actions: build mass from radius and density
convert far-field approach speed to entry speed
read the propagated uncertainty on kinetic energy
open the improvable list and choose which measurement to buy
success: The player identifies density as the dominant contributor despite its exponent of one, and reports the consequence as a range rather than a single energy.

failures.action: Buying radius because it is cubed
failures.consequence: The contribution bar barely moves; an eight per cent radius at exponent three is still smaller than a forty-five per cent density
failures.line: The exponent is not the whole story. Look at the width you are cubing.

failures.action: Reporting a single energy figure
failures.consequence: Downstream consequence modelling inherits false precision
failures.line: Give me the distribution. The clean line is what worries me.

followup.prompt: Density has the smallest exponent and dominates the uncertainty. How?
followup.answer: A term's contribution is its exponent times its fractional uncertainty; the density is known so much less well that multiplying its width by one still outweighs a small radius uncertainty multiplied by three.

assumes: fractional uncertainties combine in quadrature, weighted by exponent

title: Choose the Route That Survives Being Wrong
goal: Pick a return path that stays feasible across the consumables uncertainty, not the one that wins at the nominal.
world: four candidate trajectories on a comparison board
time, delta-v, peak heating and tracking coverage for each
a consumable-endurance slider spanning the stated uncertainty
remaining propellant, and what one later correction would cost
actions: compare the four candidates at the nominal endurance
move the endurance slider through its range and watch routes drop out
reserve propellant for at least one later correction
write an abort or reconsideration trigger before committing
success: The chosen path stays feasible under pessimistic endurance, retains propellant for a later correction, and carries a trigger that can be acted on before the options close.

failures.action: Choosing the route that wins at the nominal endurance
failures.consequence: Moving the slider to the pessimistic end makes it infeasible with no propellant to change it
failures.line: You optimized the estimate. I asked you to survive the error bar.

failures.action: Spending propellant to the nominal optimum
failures.consequence: A later tracking update arrives and there is nothing left to act on it with
failures.line: That was our last vote.

followup.prompt: What makes an abort trigger useful rather than ceremonial?
followup.answer: It is written before commitment, tied to a measurable condition, and leaves enough time and propellant to act if the condition is crossed.

assumes: an assumption with a stated range is not a value

title: Four Casualties, One Watch Team
goal: Bound what is worsening, then assign everything else with a condition that lets someone act without you.
world: four live trend displays, not four alarm lights
the watch bill, showing exactly who is available
the boat's speed, and what it costs the navigation problem
a clock that advances whether or not the player has decided
actions: read each problem as a trend and a rate, not a colour
take the first command action and assign the first available team
delegate each remaining problem with an owner, a first action and a report threshold
advance time and revise when a threshold is crossed
success: Flooding is bounded first, speed is reduced to buy navigation time, and every remaining problem has an owner, a first action and a measurable return condition.

failures.action: Sending everyone to the loudest problem
failures.consequence: Position uncertainty grows unowned and crosses the bank margin
failures.line: Who is watching the thing that is still getting worse?

failures.action: Assigning a problem with watch it
failures.consequence: No action is taken and no report arrives until the threshold has already been passed
failures.line: Watch it until what?

failures.action: Holding eight knots while the teams work
failures.consequence: The navigation time budget visibly drains during the response
failures.line: Speed is costing you the only thing you cannot make more of.

followup.prompt: What made a good delegation different from naming who was responsible?
followup.answer: It carried a first action and a threshold, so the team could act without command and command knew in advance when the problem would need attention again.

assumes: a trend and a rate say more than a current value
reducing speed converts distance margin into time

title: Fly the Manual Attitude Turn
goal: Turn ninety degrees and arrive with essentially no residual rate, on a bounded propellant budget.
world: the window reticle and sparse external cues, no attitude readout
an estimated angular rate, updating
thruster pair selection and a pulse-duration control
a propellant counter
actions: choose a thruster pair and a pulse duration to start the turn
coast without thrust, watching the target approach
commit the braking pulse before the target attitude arrives
repeat with a failed thruster quad or a different moment of inertia
success: The target attitude is reached inside tolerance with residual rate below the limit, on budget, in both inertia cases.

failures.action: Braking when the reticle reaches ninety
failures.consequence: The vehicle overshoots by the angle it travels during the braking pulse, and the recovery costs propellant
failures.line: You stopped accelerating at ninety. You did not stop rotating.

failures.action: One long pulse at full duration
failures.consequence: The rate at arrival is far too high to null inside the budget
failures.line: Everything you put in, you have to take back out.

followup.prompt: Why must the braking pulse begin before the target attitude arrives?
followup.answer: With essentially no rotational damping, angular velocity persists until an opposing torque removes it, and removing it takes the same integrated torque that created it.

assumes: angular momentum is unchanged without an external torque

title: Confirm the Motion
goal: Judge the fit by the structure in its residuals, not by its RMS.
world: the focal plane, with residual vectors drawn at each reference star
the fit RMS, prominently displayed
reference-star residuals and the asteroid's residual on the same field
two camera timestamp conventions, one of them suspect
actions: normalise the timestamps across the night
map the residual vectors over the focal plane
compare the reference-star pattern with the asteroid's residual
refit after correcting the suspect camera and re-read both RMS and pattern

structure.region: sign flips across the chip boundary

decoy.label: Alternative fit
decoy.structure: same flip, now with an added scale term absorbing it

success: The player rejects the lower-RMS fit that absorbed the pattern into a free parameter, corrects the camera, and refits to residuals that are unstructured.

failures.action: Accepting the lowest RMS
failures.consequence: The systematic is now hidden inside a fitted term and will reappear in the propagated orbit
failures.line: That number went down. The pattern did not go away.

failures.action: Deleting the largest single residual
failures.consequence: The RMS improves and the sign flip across the chip boundary is untouched
failures.line: One big residual is an event. Six small ones in a pattern are a cause.

followup.prompt: Why should a low RMS with a pattern in it worry you more than one isolated large residual?
followup.answer: A pattern means an unmodelled systematic that will bias every future prediction in the same direction, while a single outlier is one bad measurement that averages out.

assumes: a fit's residuals should look like noise if the model is complete

title: Find What the Survey Cannot See
goal: Measure your own pipeline's blind spot by pushing known objects through it and counting what comes back.
world: a synthetic population with known orbits and sizes
the survey configuration panel: depth, cadence, sky access, linking rules
a recovery display showing injected against recovered
a warning-time histogram, initially empty
actions: inject the population and run the current survey
read recovery against magnitude, solar elongation and cadence
switch configurations one at a time and re-run
compare configurations on warning time, not on total detections

recovery.blind_spot: objects approaching from the sunward direction are never recovered at any depth

success: The player finds a blind spot that depth cannot fix, and chooses the upgrade that shifts the warning-time distribution rather than the one that maximises detections.

failures.action: Choosing the deeper survey on total detections
failures.consequence: Detections rise sharply and the warning-time histogram barely moves
failures.line: More objects, same amount of notice.

failures.action: Reading the sunward gap as a low-probability direction
failures.consequence: The injected truth shows the objects were there and simply never recovered
failures.line: That is not what is out there. That is what we throw away.

followup.prompt: Why is the warning-time distribution a better measure of a survey than the number of discoveries?
followup.answer: Discovery is only valuable because it gives the downstream capabilities time to work; a survey that finds many objects late has not changed what anyone can do about them.

assumes: a detection pipeline has a selection function that can be measured

status: documented, not proposed for a format — one instance in the whole corpus
title: Find the Route When the Lights Go
goal: Learn the compartment sequence well enough to recover after an interruption.
world: the ordered compartment layout
two alternative hatches in selected spaces
one blocked route, revealed on the second pass
distinctive physical landmarks that are not answer markers
actions: walk the route once lit, identifying boundaries and transitions
return with labels removed and lighting degraded
recover after the blocked hatch by identifying the current compartment and rejoining the sequence

data.note: No shared data shape proposed. See FORMATS.md entry 19 — build this as a world feature, not a question format.

success: Machinery control is reached, and the player can say which compartment sequence let them recover.

failures.action: Counting paces
failures.consequence: A forced detour breaks the count and the error is carried onward
failures.line: Where are you now, and how do you know?

failures.action: Counting turns
failures.consequence: One blocked hatch invalidates every subsequent turn
failures.line: That was the plan for a boat with all its doors open.

followup.prompt: Why was the compartment sequence more robust than a count of paces or turns?
followup.answer: It lets the player re-establish where they are after an interruption and rejoin the sequence, instead of carrying an accumulated error through the rest of the route.

assumes: a submarine's compartments are in a fixed order along one axis
